source_notes: Bahia Blanca GasPort is served by the moored FSRU Excelerate Excelsior (idled). Excelerate Energy's own fleet page confirms Excelsior as part of its FSRU fleet (138,000 cbm, 690 MMscf/d), and Excelerate's 2024 Sustainability Report discloses that its fleet runs dual-fuel engines burning predominantly LNG/boil-off gas (95.9% of fuel mix) with MGO as backup — an operator-primary disclosure of the vessel's own onboard power generation, satisfying the FSRU-onboard convention. As a permanently moored offshore unit it has no grid connection of its own; this operator disclosure now documents that self-generation as gas-capable.

source_notes: Bahia FSRU is the moored FSRU Excelerate Sequoia (173,400 m3, delivered 2020), operating offshore/off-grid by construction. hardware_summary: OSMR (Optimised Single Mixed Refrigerant) liquefaction design: aero-derivative gas turbines driving the refrigeration compressors, paired with a conventional combined heat and power (CHP) plant and a steam-driven ammonia refrigeration plant.
source_notes: Bear Head LNG (LNG Limited's Nova Scotia export project, engineering integrated from sister project Magnolia LNG) was designed around the OSMR liquefaction process: on-site aero-derivative gas turbines mechanically drive the refrigeration compressors, and a CHP plant supplies facility power, enhanced by a steam-driven ammonia refrigeration loop. As-designed captive power on a cancelled project.

hardware_summary: Proposed on-site "Power Generation Facility" train comprising gas turbines, steam turbines, a heat recovery steam generator, and electrical generators, sized at up to ~500 MW per 12 mtpa build-out phase (up to ~1,000 MW at full 24 mtpa build-out); fed by natural gas diverted from the terminal's own feed-gas pipeline supply (~5-7% of throughput) plus recovered boil-off/end-flash gas as fuel gas. Presented as one of two co-equal, formally-investigated power-supply options (the other being BC Hydro grid electricity via a new transmission line from the Dunsmuir substation), or a combination of both; the choice was not yet finalized (pending a joint power study with BC Hydro) when the project was cancelled at the conceptual/early-FEED stage.
source_notes: Steelhead LNG's Initial Project Description, filed with the BC Environmental Assessment Office in October 2018 for the Kwispaa LNG floating (ASLNG) project at Sarita Bay, describes a fully specified on-site natural-gas-fired power generation facility (gas turbines, steam turbines, heat recovery steam generator, electrical generators) as a live, detailed design option under formal regulatory review, co-equal with a BC Hydro grid-supply option; per the shard's cancelled-proposal rule, a regulatory filing showing an as-designed spec counts as YES even though the project was cancelled before a final choice or FEED was completed.

hardware_summary: Energos Freeze (125,856 m3) is confirmed on Energos Infrastructure's own fleet page at Manzanillo, Dominican Republic, with propulsion listed as 'Steam turbine; 580 mmscf/d; dedicated high-pressure boil-off gas compressors' -- a steam-boiler-on-BOG design (boilers fired on boil-off gas via dedicated high-pressure compressors).
source_notes: The Energos Freeze FSRU (125,000 cbm) chartered to Energia 2000 exists to supply gas to two on-shore combined-cycle power plants (2x430 MW under the IDB Invest-financed 'Manzanillo Gas & Power' project, plus Energia 2000's own 414 MW SGT6-8000H combined-cycle plant) and to the national grid/other industrial users -- a documented fuel-supply-OUT relationship, not captive power. Separately, Energos Infrastructure's own fleet page names this exact vessel at Manzanillo, Dominican Republic and documents its onboard power plant as steam turbine generation with dedicated high-pressure boil-off gas compressors -- an operator-primary, vessel- and site-specific disclosure that the FSRU's own house-load generation is gas-fired, satisfying the FSRU-onboard convention.

hardware_summary: Hoegh Gallant is confirmed on Hoegh Evi's own fleet page (170,000 cbm, built 2014, at Portland Bight Jamaica for NFE); the operator's own sustainability page states fleet-wide that 'all vessels can run on natural gas, which has the lowest CO2 emissions of all commercially available marine fuels.'
source_notes: The Hoegh Gallant FSRU (170,000 cbm, built 2014, replaced the Golar Freeze in this role Nov 2021) exists to feed regasified gas to three downstream customer plants: JPS's 190 MW Old Harbour gas-fired plant, NFE's 150 MW Jamaica co-generation plant, and Jamalco's CHP -- a clearly documented fuel-supply-OUT relationship, not captive power. Hoegh Evi's own fleet page confirms this exact vessel is a current fleet asset, and the operator's sustainability page discloses fleet-wide that all vessels can run on natural gas -- the same class of operator fleet-wide disclosure already accepted for Hoegh Giant in this corpus, so the FSRU-onboard convention is satisfied, at yellow confidence (fleet-wide claim, not an engine-type-specific spec sheet).

hardware_summary: GasLog Singapore, a 155,000 cbm tri-fuel diesel-electric (TFDE) LNG carrier (built 2010), contracted for conversion to an FSU for this project -- TFDE gensets are dual/tri-fuel diesel-electric generator sets that can burn boil-off gas to produce the vessel's own electrical power (cargo pumps, cooling, hotel load) while in service; no separate onshore captive plant is documented.
source_notes: Sinolam LNG Terminal is an FSU-only project (GasLog Singapore, converted from a TFDE LNG carrier) that will 'receive, store, and send out LNG' to Sinolam Smarter Energy's (SSE) planned gas-fired power plant near Colon -- so the downstream plant itself is a customer relationship (PowerPlantsSupplied direction), but the FSU vessel's own onboard TFDE generator sets are a documented dual-fuel (gas-capable) electrical generation plant powering the vessel's own operations while moored, matching the FSRU/FSU-onboard convention (cf. Krk's BOG-fuelled DFDE module).

hardware_summary: Frame 7-class gas turbines directly shaft-drive the propane and mixed-refrigerant (MR) compression trains on operating Trains 1-3; no electricity is generated by these units. The proposed Train 4 expansion replaces this with 3x electric (E-Drive) motors, up to 75 MW each.

source_notes: Cameron LNG's operating Trains 1-3 use on-site gas turbine mechanical drive (Frame 7-class) to directly shaft-drive the propane and mixed-refrigerant refrigeration compressors. This is captive gas power under the mechanical-drive test even though no electricity is generated. The proposed Train 4 unit is a different case: its FERC-amended design replaces the gas turbines with three electric motors (up to 75 MW each) specifically to cut emissions, so Train 4 itself is NOT captive gas power.

hardware_summary: Dedicated gas-fired turbine generator at the on-site Freeport LNG Pretreatment Facility (Quintana, TX, ~3.5 mi inland from the Quintana Island liquefaction plant per EPA NPDES Statement of Basis No. TX0134056), confirmed by both Freeport LNG's own technical description and the EPA permit's equipment enumeration ('inlet separators, mercury guard beds, compressors, acid gas removal units, dehydration units, NGL recovery units, a gas turbine generator, and associated ancillary facilities'). Normally fueled by boil-off gas (BOG) piped 12" from the liquefaction plant, with a waste heat recovery unit supplying process heating to the three pretreatment trains (captive/CHP duty); the same unit is grid-interconnected and exported ~50 MW to the ERCOT grid during the Jun-Oct 2022 post-explosion outage when fed pipeline gas directly (Gas Processing News, Jul 2022). The main T1-T4 liquefaction trains remain electric-motor-driven (three GE 75 MW motors per train) and grid-fed via ERCOT/CenterPoint -- confirmed NO for mechanical drive on the trains themselves.
source_notes: CONFIRMED YES on primary/regulatory evidence, aggregators dropped as circular. Freeport's main liquefaction trains are electric-motor-driven (three GE 75 MW motors) and grid-fed via ERCOT -- a clean NO for the trains themselves, corroborated independently by EIA (Today in Energy: "Freeport LNG is the only liquefaction facility in the United States that uses electric motors instead of natural gas turbines to drive refrigerant compressors"). But the terminal's own on-site Pretreatment Facility hosts a gas turbine generator -- confirmed by EPA's NPDES Statement of Basis (No. TX0134056, an independent federal regulatory document enumerating the facility's equipment) and by Freeport LNG's own eLNG technical page (BOG piped from the liquefaction plant fuels the turbine; waste heat recovery supplies process heating to the three pretreatment trains). Gas Processing News (Jul 2022, independent trade press) documents the same unit actually running and exporting ~50 MW to ERCOT during the post-explosion outage, fed by pipeline gas directly -- confirming it is a real, operating gas-fired generator, not a paper asset, and that it is grid-interconnected (hybrid_basis: grid_export) rather than a plain islanded on-site plant. Terminal-level verdict is YES per the terminal-first / no-MW-floor standard: the pretreatment facility is part of this GEM terminal record.

But the terminal's own on-site Pretreatment Facility hosts a gas turbine generator -- confirmed by EPA's NPDES Statement of Basis (No. TX0134056, an independent federal regulatory document enumerating the facility's equipment) and by Freeport LNG's own eLNG technical page (BOG piped from the liquefaction plant fuels the turbine; waste heat recovery supplies process heating to the three pretreatment trains). Gas Processing News (Jul 2022, independent trade press) documents the same unit actually running and exporting ~50 MW to ERCOT during the post-explosion outage, fed by pipeline gas directly -- confirming it is a real, operating gas-fired generator, not a paper asset, and that it is grid-interconnected (hybrid_basis: grid_export) rather than a plain islanded on-site plant. Terminal-level verdict is YES per the terminal-first / no-MW-floor standard: the pretreatment facility is part of this GEM terminal record.

hardware_summary: Dedicated gas-fired turbine generator at the on-site Freeport LNG Pretreatment Facility (Quintana, TX, ~3.5 mi inland from the Quintana Island liquefaction plant per EPA NPDES Statement of Basis No. TX0134056), confirmed by both Freeport LNG's own technical description and the EPA permit's equipment enumeration ('inlet separators, mercury guard beds, compressors, acid gas removal units, dehydration units, NGL recovery units, a gas turbine generator, and associated ancillary facilities'). Normally fueled by boil-off gas (BOG) piped 12" from the liquefaction plant, with a waste heat recovery unit supplying process heating to the three pretreatment trains (captive/CHP duty); the same unit is grid-interconnected and exported ~50 MW to the ERCOT grid during the Jun-Oct 2022 post-explosion outage when fed pipeline gas directly (Gas Processing News, Jul 2022). The main T1-T4 liquefaction trains remain electric-motor-driven (three GE 75 MW motors per train) and grid-fed via ERCOT/CenterPoint -- confirmed NO for mechanical drive on the trains themselves.

hardware_summary: Per the 2023 MARAD deepwater port license application (Volume II, Environmental Evaluation): the offshore export platforms would have NO connection to the onshore electric grid; gas turbine generators in simple-cycle configuration would supply all facility power.
source_notes: Cancelled/withdrawn (never-built) offshore floating export project (Grand Isle LNG Operating Company, Phase 1/Phase 2 platforms) proposed off Louisiana. Though never constructed, the project reached a real regulatory design stage: its 2023 MARAD deepwater port license application explicitly states the facility would have no grid connection and would rely on simple-cycle gas turbine generators for all power — an as-designed spec that counts as YES per the brief's rule for unbuilt projects with documented engineering detail.

hardware_summary: As-designed (superseding 2013 FERC filing): direct-drive gas turbines providing mechanical shaft power to refrigeration compressors, with turbine exhaust heat recovered via HRSG/waste-heat boiler feeding a steam turbine-generator for facility electric power — superseded the project's earlier 2009 concept of a separate 420 MW South Dunes combined-cycle power plant.
source_notes: Cancelled/withdrawn (never-built) export project (Jordan Cove LNG LLC, T1-T5) at Coos Bay, Oregon. Though never constructed, the project reached a detailed FERC engineering design stage: FERC filings describe direct-drive gas turbine mechanical compression with waste-heat recovery for steam-turbine electric generation, replacing an earlier (2009) standalone 420 MW combined-cycle power plant concept (the 'South Dunes' plant). This as-designed mechanical-drive-plus-generation combination counts as YES per the brief's rule for unbuilt projects with a documented engineering design.

hardware_summary: On-site gas turbine drivers mechanically driving the refrigerant compressors of the (shelved) Lake Charles Liquefaction export trains; no on-site electricity generation -- facility electrical load is grid-fed via a new Entergy 230-kV line, with diesel-only standby gensets for emergency backup (fuel gate fails for the backup units, not the mechanical-drive turbines).
gogpt_plant: Woodside Louisiana LNG Terminal power station
source_notes: The Lake Charles Liquefaction export-train design (shelved) uses on-site gas turbines to mechanically drive the mixed-refrigerant compressors directly (shaft power, no generator) -- a mechanical-drive captive gas power arrangement. The project's own alternatives analysis explicitly considered and rejected both (a) electric-motor-driven compressors (would require >800 MW of grid electric supply) and (b) a dedicated on-site power-generation plant (single- or combined-cycle) to supply that electric-motor option, confirming the as-designed configuration is direct gas-turbine mechanical drive, not electric generation. Facility electrical (non-compression) load is supplied by a new ~19-mile 230-kV Entergy transmission line; four 4,000-kW diesel-only standby generators provide emergency backup (diesel fails the fuel gate and does not count).

hardware_summary: 2x 33 MW gas turbines per liquefaction train, directly driving the mixed-refrigerant compressors (66 MW aggregate shaft power/train); no on-site electricity generation -- the remaining 6.5 MW/train electrical load is supplied by a new switching station and 1.3-mile 230-kV Entergy transmission line.
gogpt_plant: Woodside Louisiana LNG Terminal power station
source_notes: The proposed (as-designed) Magnolia LNG export project uses on-site gas turbines to directly, mechanically drive the mixed-refrigerant compressors of each liquefaction train (66 MW aggregate shaft power/train from two 33 MW turbines) -- a mechanical-drive captive gas power arrangement. A combined-heat-and-power configuration recovering turbine waste heat to run a steam-turbine generator was studied as an alternative and explicitly ruled out ("on-site electrical power generation was ruled out in the design of the Magnolia LNG Project"); the small remaining 6.5 MW/train electrical (non-compression) load is instead supplied by a new switching station and a new 1.3-mile 230-kV transmission line to Entergy's Graywood Substation.

hardware_summary: Baker Hughes (BHGE) LM9000 aeroderivative gas turbine(s) selected 2018 for the 2x Liqui-Max FLNG vessels (24 mtpa); count/electric rating for this specific project not published (LM9000 class rated ~65-73 MW each per Baker Hughes).
terminal_name: Main Pass Energy Hub FLNG Terminal
source_notes: Global LNG Services selected Baker Hughes to supply the LM9000 gas turbine for its Main Pass Energy Hub FLNG export project (16 mi offshore Louisiana, 2x Liqui-Max vessels, 24 mtpa combined) in 2018. This is a published as-designed equipment selection for an unbuilt/cancelled project, which per SOP counts as a YES on design even though never constructed.

hardware_summary: Shuttle/regas vessels' onboard dual-fuel power-generation engines, 2 x 11,400 kW, operable in gas mode, powering onboard regasification and vessel systems (EPA deepwater-port application).
source_notes: Neptune LNG was an offshore deepwater port (Massachusetts Bay, Suez) with regasification aboard shuttle/regas vessels. The EPA deepwater-port application documents the vessels' onboard dual-fuel power-generation engines rated 2 x 11,400 kW, operable in gas mode — on-vessel gas-capable generation powering the terminal's own regas operations, the same class as the Northeast Gateway EBRV YES.

hardware_summary: Energy Bridge Regasification Vessel (EBRV) onboard MHI-supplied dual-fuel-capable boilers feeding three steam turbine generators, run on boil-off/natural gas during regasification operations to power onboard regas and vessel systems.
source_notes: Northeast Gateway is an offshore deepwater port FSRU (Massachusetts Bay, Excelerate Energy) using submerged buoy technology; the Energy Bridge Regasification Vessel (EBRV) carries onboard steam turbine generators fed by dual-fuel boilers that burn boil-off/regasified natural gas to power the vessel's regasification and auxiliary systems during operation — a confirmed onboard captive gas power arrangement per the FSRU-onboard convention.

hardware_summary: Three LM2000 gas-turbine-driven generators (95% utilization, one as backup at 5%) supply main electrical power at 13.8 kV, fueled by LNG boil-off gas recovered from storage tanks and carrier offloading via the terminal's Fuel Gas System; two diesel-engine-driven generators provide 480 VAC emergency-only backup power (diesel day tanks, tested at 5% utilization).
source_notes: Deepwater Port License Application (MARAD/USCG Docket USCG-2002-14134) for this cancelled offshore Gulf of Mexico import terminal explicitly specifies main power generation: three LM2000 gas-turbine-driven generators fueled by LNG boil-off gas, supplying electricity to operate the facility (13.8 kV). Emergency-only backup is two diesel generators. This is a primary regulatory source describing an as-designed captive power facility on an unbuilt (cancelled) terminal, satisfying the as-designed rule.
